image_description: An underwater shot of a large fish, identified as a sturgeon, swimming towards the camera in murky green water. The fish has a broad, flattened head, visible barbels near the mouth, and pectoral fins extended. The body appears elongated with visible dorsal scutes/ridges. The lighting is diffuse due to the underwater environment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly elongated and flattened. While the exact ventral position of the mouth is hard to see from this angle, the snout shape and barbel placement are consistent with a ventral mouth structure typical of sturgeons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct barbels are clearly visible hanging down on either side of the snout. Given the symmetry and typical anatomy, the presence of four is strongly implied, though only two are strictly visible. However, the visible ones match the description perfectly.
The snout tapers to a rounded point, consistent with many sturgeon species (e.g., Lake Sturgeon or White Sturgeon).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is visibly long and torpedo-shaped (fusiform), extending back into the murky background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct ridges or bumps are visible along the dorsal midline and lateral lines, consistent with the arrangement of bony scutes rather than smooth scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The heavy green color cast of the water makes it impossible to accurately judge the true base coloration (gray/brown vs black) or the contrast with the ventral surface.
The tail fin is obscured by the murkiness of the water and the angle of the fish; the posterior end of the body fades into the background before the tail structure is clearly defined.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Significant blur and loss of detail in the rear half of the fish and the background. This is likely due to the underwater medium (particulate matter) but could also mask AI generation artifacts like fusion or missing parts.
The skin texture appears somewhat smooth and plastic-like in the highlighted areas, lacking the rough, detailed texture expected of bony scutes up close, though this may be due to image resolution.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species or at least verify the class 'sturgeon' against look-alikes like paddlefish or catfish, given the visual similarities.
To check for edge bleeding between the fish and the murky water, ensuring the fins and barbels are distinct entities and not fused with the background.
To assess if the blurriness is natural underwater diffusion or AI-generated smearing/melting artifacts.

focus_areas: Scute pattern regularity along the dorsal line
Edge sharpness against the green background
